I farm this small millet plot here in the North West, same as my father did. I went to school for a few years, so I can read the bag, but I still farm the way I know works. This year I will put a little NPK if I can get it at the subsidy price, and I will spread the goat and cow droppings I gathered in the dry season. I plant my own seed I kept from last harvest — the improved millet from the agro-dealer is too costly for this small plot, and my neighbors keep their seed too. I intercrop with cowpea like always, and my wife and I will do most of the work ourselves.
